title: Smart School Cloud: use the app in a browser and sync every device
summary: Smart School App now has an online side. Schools can open the app in a browser and keep Windows and Android devices in step over the internet.
body: Smart School App was designed to work with no internet at all, and that has not changed. Smart School Cloud adds an optional online layer for schools that want it.
Open Smart School App in any browser, with nothing to install
Keep records from Windows computers and Android phones in one school copy
Send assignments online so they appear on every connected device

The school receives a school key and a short web code. On each device, open Settings, then Internet sync, enter the server address and the key, and press Sync now. People then sign in online with the school code, their own learner code or staff ID, and their PIN.
Sync is optional and off until a school manager turns it on. Local backups keep working with or without the cloud.

title: How offline sync keeps every device in step
summary: Several teachers, several computers, no reliable internet. Here is how records from different devices are merged without losing anyone's work.
body: In many schools, one teacher marks on a phone while another uses the school computer. The records must come together without one device overwriting another.

When two devices sync, Smart School App compares them record by record. The most recent change to each record wins, and records that exist on only one device are kept. Nothing is deleted just because another device has not seen it yet.
Over the school Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot, with no internet
Through a USB drive or folder backup
Online through Smart School Cloud, when a connection is available
Whichever way is used, run the same app version on every device so merges behave the same everywhere.

title: Five tips for faster lesson plans with the REB template
summary: Planning takes time. These five habits help teachers prepare clear lesson plans in less time.
body: A good lesson plan is short, clear and usable. These tips work with the official REB lesson plan template.
Start from the scheme of work. Copy the unit objectives first, then plan the activities that lead to them.
Plan backwards. Decide how you will know learners understood, then design the activities.
Reuse what works. Save a good plan and adapt it for the next class.
Write timings in minutes for each stage so the lesson fits the period.
Prepare one extension task for fast learners and one support task for those who need help.
Smart School App's lesson plan generator fills the template from the real scheme of work in English, French or Kinyarwanda, so teachers can spend their time on the teaching ideas.

title: Windows or Android? Choosing devices for Smart School App
summary: Both platforms run the same app with the same content. Here is how to decide what fits your school.
body: Smart School App runs on Windows 10 or 11 and on Android 7.0 or newer, with the same accounts, books and tools.
Best for the head teacher, the school office and the computer lab. Larger screens make timetables, gradebooks and printing easier.
Best for teachers on the move and for learners who continue at home on a family phone. Allow at least 4 GB of free storage because the library is bundled inside the app.
Most schools use both and let the devices sync over the school Wi-Fi or online through Smart School Cloud.

title: Getting more from P6 exam practice
summary: Past papers help most when learners review their mistakes. A simple routine turns practice into progress.
body: Sitting past papers is useful, but the learning happens in the review.
Practise under timed conditions once a week.
Review every wrong answer and read the model answer.
Note the topic behind each mistake and revisit that topic the next day.
Repeat the missed questions after a few days to check the learning stuck.
Smart School App marks written answers against an answer key and lists weak topics. Teachers should review and confirm each answer key on the Answer keys screen before relying on marks for grades.
